the development and validation of a novel in vivo technique that is capable of measuring the dynamic range of skeletal muscle ATP turnover rates in rats.
the development and use of (31)P MRS to investigate the role of insulin in the modulation of muscle energy metabolism and the effects of insulin resistance in obesity.

the development and use of a novel technique that can be used to assess mitochondrial function in the context of insulin resistance and to evaluate the effects of antidiabetic agents on this function.

high-fat diet induces insulin resistance, which, in turn, impairs mitochondrial activity in skeletal muscle.
the present study has demonstrated that insulin-resistant skeletal muscles of diet-induced obese rats are characterized by a blunted response to insulin in terms of ATP synthesis rate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present study demonstrates the feasibility of using in vivo saturation transfer NMR to assess insulin-stimulated mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle in a preclinical rodent model.
the insulin challenge facilitates a more accurate assessment of the effects of antidiabetic drugs on mitochondrial function in preclinical models of insulin resistance.
insulin resistance is associated with a blunted response to the insulin challenge in muscle mitochondrial ATP turnover.

in vivo (31P) saturation transfer NMR is a valuable tool for the study of mitochondrial function and insulin action in preclinical models.
in vivo saturation transfer NMR is an ideal tool to study the dynamic range of mitochondrial function in vivo and to assess the effects of pharmacological interventions in preclinical models.
